refactor(vault): implement flush-on-write pattern for reliable data persistence

Previously, vault data was only flushed on lifecycle events (app exit,
  backgrounding), which was unreliable - especially on macOS where Cmd+Q
  could terminate the app before the flush completed.

  Now, data is persisted immediately after every mutation:
  - Paired peers: flushed on pair/unpair/name update
  - Clipboard history: flushed on add/clear (if keep_history enabled)
  - Device identity: flushed on name change

  Changes:
  - Add flush helper methods to AppState (flush_paired_peers,
    flush_clipboard_history, flush_device_identity, flush_all_to_vault)
  - Refactor all data mutation points to call helpers immediately
  - Lifecycle handlers now serve as safety nets, not primary persistence
  - Remove legacy plaintext storage functions (peers.json, identity.json)
  - Clean up ~170 lines of dead code

  The lifecycle handlers (ExitRequested, Focused) still flush as a safety
  net but are no longer critical for data integrity.

fix(mobile): remove dead background notification code and add pairing UX guidance

Mobile platforms (iOS/Android) terminate network connections when the app
is backgrounded, making background pairing notifications impossible without
a central relay server (which would defeat the decentralized architecture).

Changes:
- Remove unreachable notification code from lib.rs (was never triggered)
- Add "keep app open on both devices" hints in peers view and pairing modal
- Update ARCHITECTURE.md and README.md to document this platform limitation

feat(mobile): exclude notification plugin from mobile builds

Since mobile platforms terminate network connections when backgrounded,
notifications can never be triggered. This removes the unnecessary
notification permission from mobile builds.

Changes:
- Make tauri-plugin-notification a desktop-only dependency in Cargo.toml
- Split capabilities: default.json (all platforms) + desktop.json (notifications)
- Conditionally initialize notification plugin only on desktop
- Update notifications.ts docs to explain desktop-only behavior

Benefits:
- No POST_NOTIFICATIONS permission on Android 13+
- Smaller mobile binary
- Cleaner permission list for users
